required_items.text: Provision for all hazards;

Provision for the care of residents remaining in the facility during an emergency, including pre-disaster or emergency preparation; protecting the facility; supplies; emergency power; food and water; staffing; and emergency equipment;

Provision for the care of residents who must be evacuated from the facility during an emergency including identification of such residents and transfer of resident records; evacuation transportation; sheltering arrangements; supplies; staffing; emergency equipment; and medications;
Provision for the care of additional residents who may be evacuated to the facility during an emergency including the identification of such residents, staffing, and supplies;
Identification of residents with Alzheimer's disease or related disorders, and residents with mobility limitations who may need specialized assistance either at the facility or in case of evacuation;
Identification of and coordination with the county emergency management agency;

Arrangement for post-disaster activities including responding to family inquiries, obtaining medical intervention for residents, transportation, and reporting to the county emergency management agency the number of residents who have been relocated, and the place of relocation; and,
The identification of staff responsible for implementing each part of the plan.
All staff must be trained in their duties and are responsible for implementing the emergency management plan. New staff must be trained on the plan within 30 days of employment.

The acquisition of a sufficient alternate power source such as a generator(s), maintained at the assisted living facility, to ensure that ... ambient air temperatures will be maintained at or below 81 degrees Fahrenheit for a minimum of ninety-six (96) hours in the event of the loss of primary electrical power. [The plan must include the area(s) where the temperature will be maintained, and the systems and equipment and fuel required to operate them.]

The acquisition of sufficient fuel, and safe maintenance of that fuel at the facility, to ensure that ... there is sufficient fuel available for the alternate power source to maintain ambient temperatures at or below 81 degrees Fahrenheit for a minimum of ninety-six (96) hours ... The plan must include information regarding fuel source and fuel storage.

The acquisition of services necessary to maintain, and test the equipment and its functions to ensure the safe and sufficient operation of the alternate power source maintained at the assisted living facility.
The acquisition and maintenance of a carbon monoxide alarm.

Each assisted living facility shall develop and implement written policies and procedures to ensure that the assisted living facility can effectively and immediately activate, operate and maintain the alternate power source and any fuel required for the operation of the alternate power source. ... Procedures must address the care of residents occupying the facility during a declared state of emergency, specifically, a description of the methods to be used to mitigate the potential for heat related injury including:
The use of cooling devices and equipment;
The use of refrigeration and freezers to produce ice and appropriate temperatures for the maintenance of medicines requiring refrigeration;
Wellness checks by assisted living facility staff to monitor for signs of dehydration and heat injury; and
A provision for obtaining medical intervention from emergency services for residents whose life safety is in jeopardy.

The facility's admission policy and the services the facility is prepared to provide or arrange in order to meet resident needs. [Basis for the administrator's appropriateness-of-admission determination.]
The facility's admission and continued residency criteria;
The daily, weekly or monthly charge to reside in the facility and the services, supplies, and accommodations provided by the facility for that rate;
Personal care services that the facility is prepared to provide to residents and additional costs to the resident, if any;
Nursing services that the facility is prepared to provide to residents and additional costs to the resident, if any;
Food service and the ability of the facility to accommodate special diets;
The availability of transportation and additional costs to the resident, if any;
Any other special services that are provided by the facility and additional cost if any;
Social and leisure activities generally offered by the facility;
Any services that the facility does not provide but will arrange for the resident and additional cost, if any;
The facility rules and regulations that residents must follow as described in Rule 59A-36.007, F.A.C.;
The facility policy concerning Do Not Resuscitate Orders pursuant to Section 429.255, F.S., and Rule 59A-36.009, F.A.C., and Advance Directives pursuant to Chapter 765, F.S.;

If the facility is licensed to provide extended congregate care, the facility's residency criteria for residents receiving extended congregate care services. The facility must also provide a description of the additional personal, supportive, and nursing services provided by the facility including additional costs and any limitations on where extended congregate care residents may reside based on the policies and procedures described in Rule 59A-36.021, F.A.C.;

If the facility advertises that it provides special care for individuals with Alzheimer's disease and related disorders, a written description of those special services as required in Section 429.177, F.S.; and,
The facility's resident elopement response policies and procedures.
All trained staff must adhere to the facility's infection control policy and procedures when assisting with the self-administration of medication.

The facility's rules and regulations require central storage of medication and that policy has been provided to the resident before admission as required in Rule 59A-36.006, F.A.C. [Medication central-storage policy, if the facility has one.]
Aging in place; [ECC only: the facility must develop and implement specific written policies and procedures that address:]
The facility's residency criteria developed in accordance with the admission and discharge requirements described in subsection (4), and extended congregate care services listed in subsection (7);

The personal and supportive services the facility intends to provide, how the services will be provided, and the identification of staff positions to provide the services including their relationship to the facility;

The nursing services the facility intends to provide, identification of staff positions to provide nursing services, and the license status, duties, general working hours, and supervision of such staff;
Identifying potential unscheduled resident service needs and mechanisms for meeting those needs including the identification of resources to meet those needs;
A process for mediating conflicts among residents regarding choice of room or apartment and roommate; and,

How to involve residents in decisions concerning the resident. The services must provide opportunities and encouragement for the resident to make personal choices and decisions. If a resident needs assistance to make choices or decisions, a family member or other resident representative must be consulted. Choices must include at a minimum whether:
To participate in the process of developing, implementing, reviewing, and revising the resident's service plan,

To remain in the same room in the facility, except that a current resident transferring into an extended congregate care services may be required to move to the part of the facility licensed for extended congregate care, if only part of the facility is so licensed,
To select among social and leisure activities,
To participate in activities in the community. At a minimum the facility must arrange transportation to such activities if requested by the resident; and,
To provide input with respect to the adoption and amendment of facility policies and procedures.

sections: Rule 59A-36.019 - Emergency Management: (1) Emergency plan components (a)-(h); (2) Plan approval; (3) Plan implementation; (4) Facility evacuation; (5) Emergency shelter

Rule 59A-36.025 - Emergency Environmental Control: (1) Detailed plan; (2) Submission; (3) Approved plans; (4) Implementation; (5) Policies and procedures; (6) Revocation/fines; (7) CEMP; (8) Notification
Rule 59A-36.006 - Admission Procedures: (1) Admission criteria; (2) Health assessment; (3) Admission package (a)1-14; (4) Continued residency; (5) Discharge
Rule 59A-36.021 - Extended Congregate Care Services (ECC license only): (2) ECC policies (a)-(g)

notes: Florida publishes no single policy-and-procedure checklist for ALF licensure. The AHCA ALF page lists none, and the application is filed through the AHCA online licensing system. The items above therefore come from the rule sections that list written content. Every item is quoted from the Cornell LII copy of the F.A.C. text, whose notes show the amendment dates in each document's version field. Compare against the official Florida Administrative Rules Gateway (flrules.org) before relying on it. Organization and submission: (1) The Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan must be written on AHCA Form 3180-5006 (Sept. 2023) and submitted to the county emergency management agency, which is the final administrative authority. A significant modification must be submitted within 30 days (59A-36.019(2)). (2) The emergency power plan under 59A-36.025 supplements the CEMP. A new ALF must submit and implement it before obtaining a license. After county approval, proof of approval must go to AHCA at assistedliving@ahca.myflorida.com within 30 days, along with a consumer-friendly summary. AHCA's page offers an Emergency Power Plan Sample Format. The written power policies (59A-36.025(5)) must be kept at the facility, be producible immediately, and be open to residents and their representatives. (3) The 59A-36.006(3) admission statement can be met with the resident contract or a brochure that contains all 14 items. Resident contracts must also meet Rule 59A-36.018, which was not fetched. (4) The ECC policies in 59A-36.021(2) apply only if the facility seeks an ECC license. They must be kept as a record under 59A-36.021(8)(d). LNS (59A-36.022) and LMH (59A-36.020) list no written policy topics. They set staffing, records, and per-resident plans. Not reviewed: Rules 59A-36.007 (facility rules and resident rights), 59A-36.009, 59A-36.010 (staffing), 59A-36.011 (training), 59A-36.012 to 59A-36.018, and ss. 429.28 and 429.41, F.S. These may require further written policies, such as rules and regulations, DNR, resident rights, and abuse reporting. Verify them against the rule text before finalizing the manual. The AHCA ALF survey tags PDF may also be useful, but it was not opened.
